description: An argument-type refusal is anchored on the OPERATOR TOKEN: 1-based line, 0-based position within that line. The anchor tracks the operator through a longer prefix, later lines (restarting per line), nesting, earlier select items, WHERE clauses, a CTAS body (absolute in the whole statement), the FROM-less value route, and a re-parsed view body whose offsets compose with the statement's (line included). All live-measured. Converted 1:1 from expressions/ArgumentTypeRefusalPositionTest (now retired).

SELECT bn || s AS c FROM op_t
SELECT d + d AS c FROM op_t
CREATE TABLE op_t (bn BINARY, s VARCHAR(4), d DATE, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)
SELECT     bn || s AS c FROM op_t
CREATE TABLE op_t (bn BINARY, s VARCHAR(4), d DATE, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)

SELECT
  bn || s AS c
FROM op_t

SELECT
  d
  + d AS c
FROM op_t
CREATE TABLE op_t (bn BINARY, s VARCHAR(4), d DATE, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)
SELECT UPPER(bn || s) AS c FROM op_t
SELECT (bn || s) AS c FROM op_t
CREATE TABLE op_t (bn BINARY, s VARCHAR(4), d DATE, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)
SELECT n AS a, bn || s AS c FROM op_t
SELECT n FROM op_t WHERE bn || s = 'x'
CREATE TABLE op_t (bn BINARY, s VARCHAR(4), d DATE, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE op_c AS SELECT bn || s AS c FROM op_t
CREATE TABLE op_t (bn BINARY, s VARCHAR(4), d DATE, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)
SELECT ts + n AS c FROM op_t
SELECT TO_TIMESTAMP('2026-01-01') + 1 AS c

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW op_bv_with_a_much_longer_name AS SELECT bn || s AS c FROM op_u
